app.title: Map editor
models.title: Model import
models.intro: Models loaded: {n}. Each one was converted to .glb.
models.missing: {file}: missing files: {names}. Select them together with the model (pick several files at once or pack everything into a .zip).
models.unused: {file}: skipped – not a model or a companion file.
models.noModel: None of the selected files is a model (.glb, .gltf, .fbx, .obj).
models.none: No models have been loaded yet.
tb.moveHint: Select and move objects with the gizmo arrows
tb.sculptHint: Terrain brushes: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, noise
tb.stampHint: Image stamp: mountain, crater, gorge or your own image
tb.placeHint: Place the object type last chosen in the palette
tb.lassoHint: Collision lasso: outline an area that cannot be entered
tb.lineHint: Collision line: a wall of adjustable thickness along a polyline
toast.pickType: Pick an object type in the palette first
tb.gameViewHint: Camera set up like in the game; hides editor-only objects
tb.mannequinHint: See-through character at player scale next to the cursor and the selected object – to judge proportions
palette.intro: Click a type, then the terrain to place an object. Paths and zones are drawn point by point.
terrain.targetHint: The Flatten brush moves terrain towards this height. Ctrl + click on terrain picks the height.
terrain.sculptHelp: Hold the left button and paint. Shift swaps raise and lower. Ctrl + click picks the flatten height.
terrain.baseLayer: The first layer is the base – painting with it works like an eraser
terrain.paintHelp: Pick a layer and paint. Shift + paint restores the base. Water ripples in the preview.
terrain.waterLevelHint: Height of the water surface in hollows; on higher ground water lies just above the terrain
terrain.slopeEnable: Mark slopes that are too steep as impassable
terrain.slopeHelp: Slopes steeper than the limit go into the impassable mask of the saved file. Gentler slopes can be climbed at normal speed.
list.selectGroupHint: Click to select the whole group content (Shift – add). Drag to move the group.
list.rowHint: Click to select (Shift – add). Double-click to show the object.
list.empty: The map has no objects yet.
list.groupHint: Put the selected objects and groups into a new group
list.ungroupHint: Ungroup the selected groups (or take the selected objects out of their group)
list.newGroupHint: An empty group – drag objects into it
list.treeHelp: Drag objects and groups: onto a group – inside it, onto an object – before it, onto the box at the bottom – to the top level.
list.cantMove: A group cannot be moved into itself or its subgroup
list.duplicateGroup: Duplicate the group with its content
list.ungroupThis: Ungroup (the content moves one level up)
list.dropRoot: Drop here to take out of groups
props.nothingSelected: Nothing selected. Click an object in the view or in the list.
props.multiTypes: Objects of different types – only the buttons above apply.
props.name: Name
props.baseScaleHint: The base scale belongs to the model: changing it immediately changes every copy of the model on the map. The object's scale multiplier works separately.
props.pointsHelp: Drag the white dots, double-click next to the line to add a point, Alt + click or Delete removes a point.
validation.ok: All good – the map follows the schema rules.
validation.clickHint: Click to go to the object
issue.unknownType: “{name}”: type “{type}” is not in the schema
issue.refWrongType: “{name}”: “{prop}” points to “{target}” of the wrong type ({type})
issue.pathTooShort: “{name}”: a path needs at least 2 points
issue.zoneTooShort: “{name}”: a zone needs at least 3 points
issue.outsideMap: “{name}”: the object is outside the map
issue.playerScaleMismatch: By the unit scale the player is {height} m tall (reference: {expected} m) – check scale.unitsPerMeter and player.height
issue.unknownLayer: Terrain layer “{layer}” is not in the schema
issue.schemaMismatch: The map was made for schema “{map}”, but “{schema}” is loaded
hint.select: Click an object to select it (Shift – add). Drag an object over the terrain or use the gizmo. Drag on empty space for box selection. Right button rotates the view, wheel zooms, middle button pans.
hint.vertex: Drag the point. Delete or Alt + click removes it, double-click next to the line adds a new one.
hint.sculpt.raise: Raise terrain: hold the left button (Shift – lower). [ ] changes size.
hint.sculpt.lower: Lower terrain: hold the left button (Shift – raise). [ ] changes size.
hint.sculpt.smooth: Smooth terrain: hold the left button.
hint.sculpt.flatten: Flatten to the height from the Terrain panel. Ctrl + click picks the height from the terrain.
hint.paint: Painting layer “{layer}”: hold the left button (Shift – restore base).
hint.place: Click the terrain to place “{name}”. Esc stops placing.
hint.placeNone: Pick an object type from the palette.
hint.drawPath: Drawing path “{name}” (points: {n}): click the next points, Enter or double-click finishes, Backspace removes the last point, Esc cancels.
hint.drawZone: Drawing zone “{name}” (points: {n}): click the corners, click the first point, Enter or double-click closes, Backspace removes the last point, Esc cancels.
newMap.title: New map
newMap.name: Map name
newMap.resolutionHint: More points = finer terrain detail, but a bigger file and slower brushes. 129 or 257 is usually enough.
dlg.unsavedText: The map has changes that were not saved to a file. The working copy in the browser will be replaced. Continue?
dlg.schemaMismatch: This map was made for schema “{map}”, but “{schema}” is loaded now. Load the right schema first (File → Load game schema). Open the map anyway?
dlg.schemaLoadedText: The current map now uses the new schema (check the error list). Create a new, empty map?
toast.mannequinOn: Mannequin on: character {h} tall (M turns it off)
toast.noStamp: Pick a stamp in the Terrain tab (the image is still loading or missing)
hint.stamp: Stamp “{name}”: click the terrain to imprint the shape (dragging imprints more). Shift – inverted (e.g. a valley instead of a mountain). “,” and “.” rotate, [ ] changes the size.
terrain.stampHelp: A grey image used as a height shape: bright areas raise the terrain. Click the terrain to imprint it. Size and rotation work like for brushes.
terrain.stampHeightHint: How much the brightest point of the image raises the terrain
toast.savedWithErrors: Note: the map has errors ({n}) – saved anyway
status.autosaveFailed: Working copy saving does not work
help.title: Help
help.mouse1: Left button – current tool (select, brush, place).
help.mouse2: Right button – rotate the view; Shift + right, middle or Space + left – pan.
help.mouse3: Wheel – zoom towards the cursor. Minimap in the corner: click or drag to move the camera.
help.mouse4: In game view the angle and distance are fixed, both buttons pan.
help.more: The full guide is in README.md in the repository.
sc.heightTools: Brushes: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, noise
sc.invert: Invert the brush (lower instead of raise, eraser when painting); add to selection
sc.finish: Finish drawing a path or zone
sc.deleteVertex: Delete a path or zone point
sc.focus: Center on the selection (no selection – the whole map)
sc.spacePan: Move the camera with the mouse
help.shortcutsHint: The letter in a button's corner is its shortcut. Shortcuts do not work while typing in text fields.
minimap.hint: Minimap: click or drag to move the camera
builtin.collisionZoneHint: Impassable area drawn with the lasso. Editor-only; included in the collision export.
builtin.collisionLineHint: A wall along a polyline (e.g. a cliff edge or a river bank). Editor-only; included in the collision export.
builtin.widthHint: Width of the collision wall in map units
lasso.smoothHint: How many times to round the corners of the drawn shape (0 = no smoothing)
variation.title: Random variation when placing
variation.hint: Every placed point and solid (also a decoration from the library) gets a random scale multiplier from the range and a random rotation around the vertical axis.
hint.lasso: Collision lasso: hold the left button and outline an area that cannot be entered. On release an area with draggable points is created. Esc cancels.
toast.lassoSmall: The shape is too small – outline a bigger area
toast.lassoDone: Collision area: {n} points. Drag the points to adjust the shape.
props.simplifyHint: Removes redundant points lying almost on a straight line
builtin.decorationHint: Any model from the library, with no game logic. Collision and walkability are set on the object.
builtin.flagCollisionHint: Blocks movement (model outline seen from above)
builtin.flagWalkableHint: The character can walk on the model's upward faces
sc.playMove: Move the character (relative to the camera)
sc.playMouse: Walk to the point / walk towards the cursor
sc.playOverlays: Overlays: collisions, zones and paths, names
tb.playHint: Play this map: walk around with collisions, camera as in the game
play.title: Play mode
play.controls: WASD / arrows – move · click or hold – walk · wheel – zoom · Esc – editor
play.exitHint: Back to the editor with the same camera and tools; the map does not change
play.restartHint: The character returns to the player start
play.toolbarHint: Shift + F5 – start under the cursor · C – overlays
play.noCursor: Point at the terrain to start from under the cursor
play.noStartObject: No player start of type “{type}” – starting at the map centre
play.noStartType: The schema has no start type (player.startType) – starting at the map centre
toast.schemaChanged: Schema changed (Ctrl + Z undoes). “File → Download schema” saves it to a file.
toast.projectExported: Project downloaded: map, schema and models ({n})
lib.title: Model library
lib.intro: All loaded models. Drag a model onto the map to create a decoration. Model files can also be dropped onto the editor window.
lib.examplesHint: Loads the example models from the repository (footbridge, animated character, barrel, crate)
lib.empty: The library is empty. Import models (.glb, .gltf, .fbx, .obj, .zip) or drop files onto the window.
norm.title: Model scale – size in metres
norm.intro: The editor measured the models. Choose what each model is – the editor picks a base scale so it has a typical size in metres (1 m = {upm} map units). The base scale belongs to the model and applies to all its copies; each object also has its own multiplier.
norm.hint: Range (e.g. tree 6–10 m): a model within the range stays as is, outside it gets the nearest limit. Categories and sizes can be set in the schema (scale.categories).
lib.baseScaleHint: Model base scale – applies to all its copies
lib.dragHint: Drag onto the map (decoration) · double-click – place at the view centre
lib.useAsText: Choose the model's role. The change is saved in the schema (no file editing); Ctrl + Z undoes it.
lib.folderHint: Folders organise the library; they are saved with the project.
lib.removeTitle: Remove the model from the library?
lib.removeText: {name} will disappear from the library and the working copy. Objects that use it ({n}) will show a placeholder until the model is loaded again.
lib.dropFiles: Drop model files (.glb, .gltf, .fbx, .obj, .zip) or a project .zip
lib.dropJson: Open a map (.json) with “File → Open map…”. Models and project .zip files can be dropped onto the window.
modelDlg.typeIntro: The model used for all objects of type “{name}” and its placement relative to the object's point. The change is saved in the schema.
modelDlg.playerIntro: The character model in play mode (with “idle” and “walk” animations if present) and its placement relative to the feet. The model's front is +Z. The change is saved in the schema (player section).
modelDlg.hint: Offset and rotation relative to the object's point (its base). The object also has its own rotation and scale.
props.changeTypeHint: A decoration can become an object of a schema type and back; model, position, rotation and scale stay
props.typeModelHint: Assign a model to the type: from the library, scale, rotation and offset (saved in the schema)
props.modelMissing: Model {model} is neither in the library nor next to the editor – a placeholder is shown.
